title: Digital India BHASHINI Division Conducts Multilingual AI Workshop for Haryana Vidhan Sabha to Advance Language-First Legislative Governance
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT Digital India BHASHINI Division Conducts Multilingual AI Workshop for Haryana Vidhan Sabha to Advance Language-First Legislative Governance Showcased AI-Powered Language Technologies for Inclusive, Accessible and Citizen-Centric Legislative Governance प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, conducted a Multilingual AI Workshop for officials from the Translation, Publication and Information Technology Wings of the Haryana Vidhan Sabha Secretariat. The workshop showcased AI-powered language technologies and explored their role in strengthening language-first legislative governance, enhancing multilingual legislative workflows, and enabling more inclusive, accessible and citizen-centric legislative processes. The workshop brought together Members of the Legislative Assembly, Assembly Secretariat officials and other stakeholders to explore how multilingual AI can enhance legislative workflows, improve accessibility to legislative information and enable seamless communication across languages. The session highlighted BHASHINI's vision of building Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), where language is no longer a barrier to governance and public participation. The workshop showcased BHASHINI's growing ecosystem of multilingual AI solutions, introducing participants to its core language technologies, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Neural Machine Translation (NMT), Text-to-Speech (TTS), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Transliteration and multilingual APIs. Participants were shown how these capabilities can be seamlessly integrated into government applications, digital platforms and citizen-facing services, making legislative processes more efficient and accessible. The BHASHINI team showcased live demonstrations of its AI-powered language solutions, offering participants a first-hand experience of multilingual speech recognition, translation, transcription and document-based technologies. The demonstrations highlighted how multilingual AI can support legislative documentation, language-inclusive communication, knowledge accessibility, digital record management and citizen engagement, enabling elected representatives and Assembly officials to communicate more effectively with diverse linguistic communities. The workshop also explored opportunities for leveraging language AI to strengthen legislative processes by improving multilingual access to official documents, enabling voice-first interactions and making legislative information more accessible to citizens in their preferred language. Discussions focused on how AI-powered language technologies can support the digital transformation of legislative institutions while promoting transparency, accessibility and greater public participation. Addressing the participants, Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, said highlighted BHASHINI's vision for a language-first Digital Public Infrastructure powered by multilingual AI. He emphasised the growing role of indigenous language technologies in transforming governance by ensuring that every citizen can access digital public services in the language they understand best. He also underscored the importance of collaboration between governments, technology partners and institutions to accelerate the adoption of multilingual AI across governance ecosystems. The workshop reaffirmed BHASHINI's commitment to working closely with public institutions to expand the adoption of AI-powered language technologies across governance. It marks another significant step towards enabling language-first legislative ecosystems, strengthening multilingual accessibility and making governance more inclusive, efficient and citizen-centric. Shri Rajiv Prashad, Secretary, Haryana Vidhan Sabha, said: "As legislative institutions embrace digital transformation, technology must strengthen accuracy, efficiency, and transparency without compromising the integrity of official records. AI-enabled tools can significantly simplify transcription, translation, and documentation, while human expertise and validation remain indispensable in preserving the quality and authenticity of legislative proceedings." Hon'ble Speaker, Haryana Vidhan Sabha, Shri Harvinder Kalyan, said: "Artificial Intelligence should empower human intelligence, not replace it. By responsibly adopting voice-first multilingual technologies, legislative institutions can enhance efficiency, strengthen documentation, and improve citizen accessibility, while ensuring that human judgment, discipline, and accountability remain at the core of every official process." Shri Ram Narayan Yadav, Advisor to the Hon'ble Speaker, Haryana Vidhan Sabha, said: "The presentation on using BHASHINI AI for transcribing the proceedings of the Legislative Assembly and for the translation of its documents was extremely useful. For the accuracy of transcription, the Publication Wing will have to pay special attention to facts and language, while for translation, special attention must be given to grammar and the selection of appropriate words, so that both tasks can be carried out with complete accuracy." Amitabh Nag,CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division said: "India's legislatures generate knowledge that shapes governance and democracy. By enabling voice-first, multilingual AI, BHASHINI is helping legislative institutions make their day-to-day operations faster, more inclusive, and more accessible. From real-time transcription and translation to multilingual publication, document management, and citizen engagement, our vision is to empower every Secretariat with AI that works seamlessly across Indian languages. Our collaboration with the Haryana Vidhan Sabha is another step towards building technology that strengthens legislative efficiency while ensuring that language is never a barrier to governance." About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. Today, BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 8 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 20 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, making Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI. **** Dr. Nayan Solanki / Kanishk Sharma / Vanshita Jaiswal (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290076) आगंतुक पटल  : 150 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Electronics & IT Digital India BHASHINI Division Conducts Multilingual AI Workshop for Haryana Vidhan Sabha to Advance Language-First Legislative Governance Showcased AI-Powered Language Technologies for Inclusive, Accessible and Citizen-Centric Legislative Governance प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Public Consultations on Budget, NEP, Data Protection and Aadhaar Reforms Bring Citizens Closer to Policy Making
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT Public Consultations on Budget, NEP, Data Protection and Aadhaar Reforms Bring Citizens Closer to Policy Making Over 6.32 Crore Citizens Participate in Governance Through MyGov प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi MyGov platform was launched by the Government of India as a citizen engagement platform. It collaborates with multiple Government bodies/ Ministries to engage people in policy formulation and seeks the opinion of people on issues/ topics of public interest and welfare. For citizen engagement, the platform facilitates multiple features such as discussions, creative tasks, polls, surveys, and on-ground activities. The MyGov platform has seen significant growth in its user base and engagement metrics. It has continued to actively host Consultations (Discussions), Polls, Surveys across key national initiatives, ensuring sustained citizen participation in governance as depicted below: Sl. No. Metric Count 1 Total Citizens registered on MyGov platform (till 10.07.2026) 6,32,16,167 2 Citizens registered during last five years (11.07.2021-10.07.2026) 4,48,10,119 3 Number of “Discussions’ hosted on MyGov (last five years) 180 4 Number of citizens participated in “Discussions’ 7,77,068 5 Number of “Polls” conducted on MyGov (last five years) 15 6 Number of citizens participated in ‘Polls” 30,39,127 7 Number of “Surveys’ conducted on MyGov (last five years) 56 8 Number of citizens participated in “Surveys” 3,57,431 MyGov serves as a facilitative platform for citizen participation. Discussions and other engagement activities on the platform are owned and proposed by various Ministries and Departments. Once these consultations are concluded, the compiled opinions and suggestions are shared with the concerned ministry/department for their consideration during formulating or reviewing policies, schemes, or programmes. A few of the recent public consultations hosted on the platform include National Education Policy (NEP)-2020, Digital Personal Data Protection Bill-2022 and Draft Digital Personal Data Protection Rules-2025, Union Budget Consultations, Draft Amendments to the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules-2020, Reforms in the Examination Process (National Testing Agency), Draft Data Centre Policy-2020 and Draft New Textiles Policy-2020, Memorandum for the 8th Central Pay Commission. The final examination, acceptance, and incorporation of citizen suggestions into Government policies, programmes, or administrative actions remain the prerogative of the respective Ministries and Departments. To assess the effectiveness of its citizen engagement initiatives, third-party Impact Assessment studies have been carried out in 2017 and 2025. These studies concluded that MyGov has significantly expanded the scope of public participation through its diverse engagement models. Based on the recommendations of these assessments to improve inclusivity and accessibility, MyGov has implemented several strategic enhancements: ● Multilingual Support: The platform has been made available in 12 languages (English and 11 Indian regional languages) to bridge linguistic barriers ● Mobile Accessibility: A dedicated MyGov mobile application was launched to cater to the large number of mobile users in the country ● Enhanced Outreach: Digital and social media presence has been strengthened to ensure governance remains transparent and result-oriented ● Platform Usability: The web interface is periodically updated to enhance user experience and general accessibility MyGov compiles the feedback /suggestions/recommendations of citizens and forward these to the concerned ministries/departments for their necessary action. Decisions regarding Action Taken Reports and any consequential policy or programme changes fall within the jurisdiction of the respective ministries/departments that own the specific policy/programme/scheme. MyGov periodically reviews feedback specifically related to the functioning of its platform. This ensures that features, multilingual support, and general accessibility are continuously improved to meet the evolving needs of citizens and maintain a robust bridge between the Government and the public. title: Safe & Trusted AI Pillar under IndiaAI Mission Strengthens Citizen Trust through Secure, Fair and Responsible AI Solutions
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT Safe & Trusted AI Pillar under IndiaAI Mission Strengthens Citizen Trust through Secure, Fair and Responsible AI Solutions 13 Responsible AI Projects, 58 AI Centres of Excellence and 27 India Data & AI Labs Strengthen Safe & Trusted AI under IndiaAI Mission India's Safe & Trusted AI Pillar Powers Responsible Innovation while Shaping Global AI Governance प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi IndiaAI Mission: India’s AI policy is based on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of democratizing technology. It is aimed at creating economic opportunities and employment for youth, while addressing risks associated with AI. Accordingly, the Government approved the IndiaAI Mission in March 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,371 crore over five years to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem in the country. The Mission comprises seven pillars viz. IndiaAI Compute, Foundation Models, AIKosh, IndiaAI Application Development Initiative, FutureSkills, Startup Financing, and Safe & Trusted AI. Progress under IndiaAI mission till date: AI models: Government of India is supporting Indian startups and institutions to develop large language models. 20 indigenous sovereign model proposals have been identified for support, comprising 12 LLMs and 8 SLMs. Notable successes so far include: Sarvam AI’s Sarvam 30 billion parameter and 105 billion parameter models Gnani.AI’s speech-to-speech model BharatGen’s multilingual foundation models Avataar AI’s video generation model Domain-specific SLMs, including specialized models and AI frameworks addressing healthcare, language technologies and agentic AI systems are at various stages of development and deployment. Affordable compute: Compute service providers empanelled: 15 Number of projects supported: 237 GPU hours sanctioned: 93 lakh GPU hours Application Development: 12 National-level Hackathons/Innovation Challenges launched. Supported the development of 62 AI prototypes and 20 AI solutions deployment Talent development: 686 fellowships have been awarded across undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes in 178 institutions. YUVA AI for All programme has been completed by over 26 lakh individuals. IndiaAI labs: 27 India Data and AI Labs have been established, which has supported training for more than 2500 students Work ongoing on additional 188 labs. AI Centres of Excellence: 58 Artificial Intelligence Centres of Excellence (AI-CoEs) being established across States and Union Territories in collaboration with the respective State/UT Governments and industry partners. Safe & Trusted AI pillar At the same time, the Government is also cognizant of the risks associated with AI. The Safe & Trusted AI pillar of the IndiaAI Mission aims to promote the responsible development, deployment and adoption of AI through indigenous governance frameworks, standards, tools and evaluation mechanisms. 13 Responsible AI projects have been approved in educational institutions across the country. These include topics such as bias mitigation, machine unlearning, privacy-preserving AI, explainability, deepfake detection and AI risk assessment. Key initiatives include: Saakshya, multi-agent framework developed by IIT Jodhpur &  IIT Madras for deep fake detection AI Vishleshak for improving Audio-Visual forgery detection system IIT Kharagpur’s project on Real-Time Voice Deepfake Detection System Nature & Objectives of projects related to bias mitigation, explainability, privacy preserving Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning: Bias Mitigation: NIT Raipur is developing responsible AI algorithms to reduce bias in medical image analysis, clinical decision-making and healthcare applications Privacy-Preserving & Explainable AI: IIT Delhi (with IIIT Delhi and IIT Dharwad) is developing privacy-preserving machine learning models using federated learning. Defence Institute of Advanced Technology (DIAT) is is building explainable & privacy-preserving AI for security applications Machine Unlearning: IIT Jodhpur is developing techniques to remove remove unwanted, sensitive or outdated information/concepts from generative foundation models Overall, these projects are aimed at making AI fairer, more transparent, privacy-preserving, secure and trustworthy. •  The AI Safety Institute has been established for AI safety, security and developing trust with diverse stakeholders, engaging academia, startups, industry and Government bodies through a hub-and-spoke model. • The India AI Governance Guidelines lay down a risk-based governance framework addressing algorithmic bias, misinformation, deepfakes and unintended societal harm, and propose institutional mechanisms including the AI Governance and Economic Group (AIGEG), Technology and Policy Expert Committee (TPEC) and AI Safety Institute (AISI) for oversight, standards and safety research. The IndiaAI Safety Institute was announced in January 2025 to advance science-based and indigenous research on AI safety and governance. The Institute is responsible for promoting the safe, secure, inclusive and trustworthy development, deployment and adoption of AI in India. It also oversees the implementation of projects selected under the two rounds of Expressions of Interest (EoIs) under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar. India's approach to responsible AI is anchored in the vision of "AI for All". It seeks to harness AI for inclusive development while ensuring that it remains safe, trusted, and aligned with India's socio-economic priorities. India actively engages with global processes on AI governance, including Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI), G20, and United Nations, to ensure that international norms reflect the perspectives and priorities of the Global South As Chair of the India AI Impact Summit 2026, held in New Delhi, India contributed in shaping the global agenda on responsible AI through key deliverables: As part of New Delhi Frontier AI Impact Commitments, leading AI developers made voluntary commitments on the safe and responsible development of frontier AI Guidance Note on AI Governance, oﬀered practical guidance to countries on designing context-appropriate AI governance frameworks Trusted AI Commons, a shared repository of open resources to democratise access to safe and trusted AI These outcomes reflect India's commitment to shaping global norms on AI governance while protecting its strategic and developmental interests. This information was submitted by Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in Rajya Sabha on 24.07.2026. **** Dr. Nayan Solanki / Kanishk Sharma / Vanshita Jaiswal (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289946) आगंतुक पटल  : 222 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Kannada Ministry of Electronics & IT Safe & Trusted AI Pillar under IndiaAI Mission Strengthens Citizen Trust through Secure, Fair and Responsible AI Solutions 13 Responsible AI Projects, 58 AI Centres of Excellence and 27 India Data & AI Labs Strengthen Safe & Trusted AI under IndiaAI Mission India's Safe & Trusted AI Pillar Powers Responsible Innovation while Shaping Global AI Governance प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INDIA’s NDC TARGETS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INDIA’s NDC TARGETS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi India's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) comprises three quantitative targets namely the reduction of overall emission intensity of our GDP, enhancing share of non-fossil fuel-based energy resources in installed electric power capacity and creation of additional carbon sink. India has achieved a reduction of 37.38% in the emissions intensity of its GDP in 2022 from the 2005 level, against the NDC goal of reducing emissions intensity by 45% by 2030. The share of cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel-based sources crossed 50% in June 2025, thereby achieving the NDC goal five years ahead the committed timeline. As of 30th June 2026, non-fossil fuel-based energy resources accounted for 54.18% of the country's total installed electric power capacity. India has created an additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent during 2005 to 2022, against the NDC goal of creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2030 through additional forest and tree cover. The NDC targets for the year 2035 have been enhanced, with quantitative targets to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 47% from the 2005 level, achieve 60% cumulative installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources, and create carbon sink of 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest and tree cover as compared to the baseline year of 2005. The NDC also includes five qualitative targets aimed at promoting sustainable lifestyles, adoption of climate friendly and cleaner path and enhancing adaptation capacity, etc. aligned with the goal of Viksit Bharat @2047. Our goal is to achieve the NDC targets at the national level, in line with the provisions of the Paris Agreement which calls for nationally determined contributions and national level reporting from the signatory Parties. The Government of India stands committed to implement its climate commitments through a whole-of-government approach. The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) comprises of nine national missions in specific areas of agriculture, energy efficiency, green India, Himalayan eco-system, human health, solar energy, strategic knowledge on climate change, sustainable habitat, and water. Six of its nine missions focus on adaptation for enhancing climate resilience of vulnerable communities. All these missions are institutionalized and implemented by their respective Nodal Ministries/Departments through various schemes and programs across many sectors. Several measures have been taken to accelerate climate mitigation and adaptation under these schemes and programs. The focus is to promote renewable energy, electric mobility, sustainable transport and habitats; climate resilient agriculture; water conservation; enhance energy efficiency; forest and tree cover; restore ecosystems; reduce disaster risks, etc. Some of the flagship initiatives are National Green Hydrogen Mission; PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana; Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM); Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for clean energy technologies, including high-efficiency solar PV modules and Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries; initiatives related to Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) and Nuclear Energy Mission; and launch of hydrogen powered train which is step forward towards future ready and low-carbon sustainable transport. For coastal regions, measures include, inter-alia, conservation and restoration of mangroves and coastal ecosystems, implementation of the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) regulatory framework, strengthening of early warning systems and disaster preparedness, and promotion of nature-based and ecosystem-based approaches to enhance resilience against cyclones, coastal flooding, sea-level rise and coastal erosion. The Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI) programme, along with other initiatives under the National Coastal Mission, contribute to the conservation and restoration of mangroves and strengthening the resilience of coastal ecosystems and communities. Further, aligned with NAPCC, 34 States and Union Territories have prepared their respective State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs), which facilitate climate action based on State/UT-specific vulnerabilities, priorities and circumstances. The Government has institutional mechanisms to monitor progress towards India's NDC targets and the long-term goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070. The Prime Minister's Council on Climate Change (PMCCC), Executive Committee on Climate Change (ECCC) and Apex Committee for Implementation of the Paris Agreement (AIPA) oversee the implementation of domestic climate actions, with periodic inputs from concerned Ministries and Departments. In addition, implementation of climate commitments is undertaken in convergence with relevant Government schemes, programmes and sectoral policies, which have inbuilt monitoring and reporting mechanisms. India also tracks and reports progress, as per the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) under the Article 13 of the Paris Agreement, through its Biennial Transparency Reports, and National Communications, supported by national monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) arrangements. This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today. ***** VM/GS (Lok Sabha US Q1291) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289995) आगंतुक पटल  : 216 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INDIA’s NDC TARGETS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: TREE FELLING AND TIMBER TRANSIT FRAMEWORK
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: TREE FELLING AND TIMBER TRANSIT FRAMEWORK प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi The felling of trees and issuance of transit permits for timber grown under agroforestry is regulated by the respective State Governments under the provisions of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, State-specific Forest Acts, State specific Tree management Acts, rules made thereunder, and orders of the Hon'ble Courts. The list of exempted tree species, as well as the procedures and documentation required for obtaining felling and transit permits, vary from State to State, depending upon the applicable State-specific Acts, rules and directions of the Hon'ble Courts. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has issued various guidelines and advisories to States and Union Territories for liberalising the transit and felling regulations for promoting agroforestry. The Ministry has revised the Wood Based Industries (Establishment and Regulation) guidelines in 2022 to liberalize the regulations relating to setting up of Wood-based Industries using species grown under agroforestry. The Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE) has been continuously pursuing tree improvement programs to promote agroforestry. So far, ICFRE has released 69 varieties and clones that are being widely planted by farmers, forest departments, forest development corporations and wood-based industries in agro forestry and social forestry programmes. title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: COMMUNITY-LED TREE PLANTATION DRIVES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: COMMUNITY-LED TREE PLANTATION DRIVES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi The Government has undertaken several measures to address the impacts of extreme summer heatwaves and rising temperatures. The National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) enlists 17 major hazards, including Heat Waves. It prescribes a comprehensive responsibility matrix delineating the roles and responsibilities of Central Ministries/Departments, State Governments through the State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs), District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs), local authorities and other stakeholders for prevention, preparedness, mitigation, response and recovery. The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) issued the Guidelines on Preparation of Action Plan for Prevention and Management of Heat Wave in 2016, which were revised in 2019. The Guidelines facilitate heat wave-prone States/Union Territories (UTs) in preparing State, District and City Heat Action Plans (HAPs) for effective management of heat wave conditions. The Guidelines provide for vulnerability assessments to identify vulnerable populations, including the elderly, children, outdoor workers, the urban poor and others at-risk groups, and prescribe appropriate mitigation and preparedness measures. Recognising the growing impact of urbanisation on heat stress, the Guidelines also provide for assessment of the built environment to identify factors contributing to the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect and recommend integration of long-term heat mitigation measures into urban planning and development, including enhancement of green cover, promotion of cool roofs and cool pavements, preservation of water bodies, improved ventilation corridors, and adoption of climate-responsive building and land-use practices. The NDMP and the Guidelines specify the roles and responsibilities of various Central Ministries, State Governments and local authorities for addressing the challenges faced by outdoor workers and people residing in informal urban settlements. Accordingly, all heat wave-prone States, including Bihar and Madhya Pradesh, have prepared and are implementing their respective State Heat Action Plans. Further, under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) and AMRUT 2.0, parks, green spaces and urban water bodies are developed to enhance urban climate resilience, including in Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. Under the AMRUT Mitra initiative, Women Self Help Groups undertake tree plantation and maintenance of parks and green spaces. In addition, under the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SSASCI) Scheme, urban greening initiatives are supported, including development of urban greens in Bihar. The Government is also implementing Nagar Van Yojana (NVY) which envisages developing 600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas in the country during the period of 2020-21 to 2026-27. The objective is to significantly enhance the tree outside forests and green cover, enhancement of biodiversity and ecological benefits to the urban and peri-urban areas apart from improving quality of life of city dwellers. The Central grants from funds under National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) are provided under the scheme to cover mainly the cost of fencing, soil-moisture conservation measures & related activities, administrative activities, plantation and maintenance. Under the India Cooling Action Plan (ICAP), the Government promotes passive cooling in buildings through adoption of the Energy Conservation and Sustainable Building Code (ECSBC) for commercial and office buildings and residential buildings. The code emphasizes energy-efficient building envelopes and cross-ventilation strategies to reduce cooling demand and improve the overall energy performance of new buildings. The Government also promotes community participation in tree plantation and enhancement of green cover through various initiatives, including 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' to encourage citizens to plant trees as a tribute to their mothers and to promote mass participation in tree plantation activities. Besides, tree plantation is also carried out by other Ministries, NGOs, Private sector etc. This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today. ***** VM/GS (Lok Sabha US Q1183) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289994) आगंतुक पटल  : 99 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: COMMUNITY-LED TREE PLANTATION DRIVES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: STREET VENDORS UNDER PM SVANIDHI
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs STREET VENDORS UNDER PM SVANIDHI प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme was launched on 01 st June 2020.  Under the scheme, till 12 th July 2026, 76.95 lakhs street vendor have availed 1.15 crore loans amounting to ₹18475.06 Crore. Under the scheme, working capital term loans are provided to the street vendors in three tranches of upto ₹15,000, ₹25,000, and ₹50,000 to be repaid in 12 months, 18 months, and 36 months respectively through monthly instalments. Therefore, repayment varies accordingly.State-wise details are available on PM SVANidhi portal https://pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in Since scheme inception till 12 th July 2026, the number of street vendors who have availed the second and third tranches of loans under the scheme are 29,71,195 and 8,49,471 respectively. SVANidhi se Samriddhi’ component under the PM SVANidhi Scheme, was launched on 04 January, 2021, to build social security net for the beneficiaries’ families for improving their living conditions. This facilitates linkages to 8 select Central Government Welfare schemes designed to provide a safety net and social security for the eligible beneficiaries and their families. As on 12th July 2026, socio economic profiling is completed for 50.63 lakh PM SVANidhi beneficiaries along with 1.06 crore family members and a total of 1.56 crore scheme sanctions have been extended to them. Impact assessment studies of the PM SVANidhi scheme was undertaken by Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad in 2023 & 2025. The 2023 study was conducted in 100 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries and it found that PM SVANidhi was the first loan from a bank for 95% of the beneficiaries and the loan was utilized for expanding their business. The 2025 study was conducted in 99 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries (with around 60% of the respondents being part of the 2023 study sample) and it found that the average annualized business income among SVANidhi borrowers grew by around 20 percent, between 2023 and 2025. Around 30 percent of borrowers across all cycles reported holding loans other than PM SVANidhi loans which underscores the scheme’s role in building credit histories for vendors who previously had little or no access to formal credit. Further the study also found that between 2023 and 2025, the adoption of digital payments among street vendors rose significantly. The study also found the scheme’s impact extends well beyond business recovery. By easing credit constraints and stabilizing household cash flows, the scheme has enabled vendor families to improve living conditions, strengthen food security, enhance access to health-care, and support children’s education. This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289997) आगंतुक पटल  : 217 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs STREET VENDORS UNDER PM SVANIDHI प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ENSURING ADEQUATE PADESTRIAN INFRASTRUCTURE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs ENSURING ADEQUATE PADESTRIAN INFRASTRUCTURE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi As per 12 th Schedule of the Constitution of India, construction and maintenance of municipal roads, bridges, and associated pedestrian footpaths falls within the domain of State Governments, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and Urban Development Authorities (UDAs). The Government of India supplements these efforts through model regulations, technical standards, guidelines and advisories, and has undertaken several policy and programmatic initiatives to ensure adequate pedestrian infrastructure, enhance public transport mobility, improve last-mile connectivity, reduce traffic congestion, and promote integrated, sustainable and efficient urban transport systems across the country. The Government has issued the National Urban Transport Policy (2006) , Metro Rail Policy (2017) , Transit Oriented Development (ToD) Policy (2017) , and other policy guidelines to assist States/UTs/ULBs in the planning, developing, and managing urban transport systems. The advisory URDPFI Guidelines specifically provide for footpaths along all roads under Section 8.2.3. These frameworks promote an integrated, multimodal and people-centric approach to urban mobility, with emphasis on seamless connectivity, public transport and non-motorized transport. In addition, national missions and schemes such as the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT), the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SSASCI) and the Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines, 2014, support States/UTs/ULBs in developing adequate and safe pedestrian infrastructure. Under the AMRUT scheme, launched in 2015, 500 cities (now 485, including 15 merged cities) were selected with a focus on developing basic urban infrastructure, with non‑motorised urban transport identified as one of the components. Implementation of 346 Green Mobility projects under AMRUT has promoted environment friendly modes of transport and infrastructure, resulting in the creation of about 474.34 km of walkways and cycle tracks. Under AMRUT 2.0, launched in 2021, AMRUT Mitra initiative in convergence with the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), Women Self‑Help Groups have been involved in tree plantation and maintenance. Under this initiative 2,958 projects for tree plantations and maintenance have been approved. As per status updated by the States/ UTs on AMRUT 2.0 portal, around 7.74 lakh trees have been planted which will help in reducing pollution in cities/towns. Under Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SSASCI) scheme, Cities and ULBs have been encouraged to undertake climate sustainability initiatives under urban planning to develop walkable safe streets and footpaths. During SSASCI 2023–26, several cities have undertaken street pedestrianization reforms, and 39 Transit Oriented Development (TOD) corridors have been notified (Draft/Final) in eight States, enabling higher FAR/floors, increasing density within TOD zones and supporting improved last‑mile connectivity. As an outcome of these reforms, 22 streets with a total length of about 63.73 km have been pedestrianized in 10 States, contributing to safer, more climate‑resilient and people‑centric urban mobility. Urban transport is primarily a State subject. The Central Government continues to provide policy guidance and financial assistance through various schemes and initiatives to support States/UTs in developing integrated and efficient public transport systems. Under the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme , the Government has sanctioned 10,000 electric buses across more than 100 cities to augment city bus services, improve public transport accessibility, strengthen first- and last-mile connectivity, encourage greater use of public transport, and promote sustainable, clean, energy-efficient urban mobility and contributes to reducing dependence on private vehicles. This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289999) आगंतुक पटल  : 93 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs ENSURING ADEQUATE PADESTRIAN INFRASTRUCTURE प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ENHANCING URBAN HOUSING THROUGH PMAY-U 2.0 IMPLEMENTATION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs ENHANCING URBAN HOUSING THROUGH PMAY-U 2.0 IMPLEMENTATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been implementing Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) since 25.06.2015 to provide all weather pucca houses with basic civic amenities to eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY-U, MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY-U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas across the country to support 1 crore additional eligible beneficiaries. PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS). The Scheme Guidelines may be accessed at https://pmay-urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-2.pdf . PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 adopts a demand driven approach and no target has been fixed by the Government. States/Union Territories (UTs) assess the requirement through their Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/Implementing Agencies in their respective jurisdictions. Eligible citizens are also allowed to apply through Unified Web Portal of PMAY-U 2.0 with all details on the portal. States/UTs/ULBs validate the beneficiaries as per the eligibility criteria of the scheme guidelines and selection/scrutiny of beneficiary lists are done by the States/UTs. The Scheme Guidelines and Unified Web Portal for submitting the online applications can be accessed through https://pmay-urban.gov.in . Based on the demand survey and selection of beneficiaries, the project proposals are prepared and approved by the State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) headed by the Chief Secretary of States/UTs for further consideration of release of Central Assistance by the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC). Based on the project proposal submitted by States/UTs, a total of 127.68 lakh houses including 16.20 lakh under PMAY-U 2.0 have been sanctioned by the Ministry, so far. Out of which, 121.03 lakh houses have been grounded and 99.07 lakh are completed/ delivered to the beneficiaries across the country as on 13.07.2026.  A total of 45,982 houses including 2,120 under PMAY-U 2.0 have been sanctioned for UT of Jammu & Kashmir so far, of which 43,907 have been grounded and 35,961 completed. UT Government is encouraged to further submit the proposals for houses as per the Scheme Guidelines to achieve saturation. MoHUA launched Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHCs) as a sub-scheme of PMAY-U in July 2020 to address the housing need faced by migrant workers, urban poor and informal sector labourers from Economically Weaker Section (EWS)/Low Income Group (LIG) category across the country. This scheme has been implemented through two models. Under Model-1, a total of 336 units of houses has been converted into the ARHCs in Jammu & Kasmir. Further, based on the learnings of ARHCs, a dedicated vertical of Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) has been provisioned under PMAY-U 2.0. The Scheme Guidelines of PMAY-U 2.0 are available at https://pmay-urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-2.pdf . ARH vertical of PMAY-U 2.0 aims to promote construction of affordable rental housing close to the workplaces of the intended beneficiaries including urban migrants/ industrial workers/working women/students/urban poor etc. The ARH vertical is implemented through two models: Model-1: Converting existing Government funded vacant houses into ARH through Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode or by Public Agencies. Model-2: Construct, Operate and Maintain rental housing by Private/Public Entities for urban poor, working women, employees of Industries, Industrial Estates, Institutions and other eligible EWS/LIG families. title: How Madanapalle is building a Zero Waste City
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs How Madanapalle is building a Zero Waste City प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 3:01PM by PIB Delhi Driven by the vision of Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, Madanapalle Municipality is reshaping urban sanitation through scientific waste management and sustainable resource recovery. Madanapalle Municipality in Andhra Pradesh is strengthening its urban sanitation and solid waste management systems through scientific and sustainable practices. In response to rapid urban growth and increasing waste generation, the municipality has adopted a structured and integrated approach focused on waste segregation, scientific processing and resource recovery, with the objective of developing Madanapalle into a ‘Zero Waste City.’ Madanapalle generates approx.. 62 TPD of municipal solid waste, including 25.50 TPD of dry waste, 36 TPD of wet waste and 0.50 TPD of domestic hazardous waste. To ensure efficient management of this waste stream, a systematic source segregation mechanism has been implemented across the town. Waste is categorized into biodegradable, non-biodegradable and upcycling waste, facilitating scientific processing, improved recycling practices and environmentally sustainable disposal in alignment with the objectives of SBM-U 2.0. A major focus area for the municipality has been scientific management of biodegradable waste through decentralized and sustainable practices. Bulk Waste Generators are being encouraged to establish on-site composting systems, while citizens are adopting home composting and terrace gardening to manage wet waste at source. Every day, nearly 15.50 tonnes of wet waste is processed through windrow composting at the municipal compost yard, generating around 4.65 tonnes of compost used for parks, plantations, and gardening activities across the town. Additionally, around 3 tonnes of wet waste is processed daily through vermi composting, producing nearly 1.20 tonnes of nutrient-rich compost, further reducing landfill burden and promoting sustainable waste utilization. Dry waste generated in the town is systematically segregated into recyclable and non-recyclable categories at the doorstep level. Recyclable materials are sent to the Material Recovery Facility (MRF), where they are processed and channelled to authorized recycling units for resource recovery. Non-recyclable waste is transported to cement factories for co-processing. This initiative not only improves waste utilization efficiency but also helps generate additional revenue for the municipality. By ensuring proper segregation at source, Madanapalle has enhanced the calorific value of recyclable waste and minimized the quantity of mixed waste reaching disposal sites. Through door-to-door collection drives and the operational Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (RRR) Centre, the municipality collects items such as e-waste, old clothes, toys, books, and footwear. These materials are repaired, reused, or redistributed among slum communities, homeless individuals, and old age homes. The city has also adopted creative waste-to-art initiatives using discarded tyre waste. Public spaces and parks are being beautified with artistic installations made from waste materials, promoting environmental awareness while contributing to the vision of zero dumping. Madanapallehas successfully remediated nearly 36,512 metric tonnes of legacy waste through bio-mining and bio-remediation, reclaiming around 9.40 acres of land. Nearly 5 acres of the reclaimed area has been developed through plantation activities, transforming former dumpsites into green urban spaces. Recovered materials such as Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) are being sent to cement plants for co-processing, while soil and inert materials are reused for filling low-lying areas, promoting scientific waste utilization and environmental improvement. Wall paintings and murals promoting cleanliness, waste segregation, and hygiene have transformed public spaces into vibrant awareness platforms. The Waste-to-Art Park at NVR Layout stands as a symbol of innovation and sustainability, showcasing how discarded materials can be creatively repurposed into functional and aesthetic public installations. Aligned with the vision of the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, Madanapalle is steadily progressing towards becoming a Zero Dump and Zero Littering City through strong administrative leadership, scientific waste management systems, and active community participation. The municipality’s integrated approach—encompassing composting, recycling, upcycling, biomining, legacy waste remediation, and citizen engagement—demonstrates how urban local bodies can build sustainable and environmentally responsible cities. *** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289853) आगंतुक पटल  : 700 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs How Madanapalle is building a Zero Waste City प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission and Transfer of Rural Water Supply Schemes
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti Extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission and Transfer of Rural Water Supply Schemes From 16.71% to 82.09%: Jal Jeevan Mission Transforming Rural Tap Water Coverage 15.89 Crore Rural Households Connected to Functional Household Tap Connections Under JJM प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi To enable every rural household in the country to have assured potable water, in adequate quantity ( 55 litres per capita per day ) of prescribed quality ( BIS:10500 ) on regular and long-term basis, through tap water connection, since August 2019, Government of India in partnership with states, has been implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) - Har Ghar Jal. 'Jal Arpan' is being organized as a community-led public event with active participation of elected representatives, Gram Sabhas and local communities to celebrate successful commissioning of water supply schemes and promote long-term sustainability of rural water infrastructure. To promote Jan Bhagidari for sustainable and continuous service delivery under the JJM, a standardized “ Handbook on Community-Managed Piped Water Systems ” has been launched under the Jal Arpan initiative. The handbook mandates a 15-day trial run involving Gram Panchayats (GPs)/ Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs)/ Pani Samiti members to ensure smooth handover of water supply schemes and sustainable operations. Significant progress has been made in the country since the launch of JJM towards enhancing access to tap water to rural households. At the time of announcement of Jal Jeevan Mission, 3.23 Crore (16.71%) rural households were reported to have tap water connections. So far, as reported by States/ UTs as on 18.07.2026, around 12.66 Crore additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 18.07.2026, out of 19.36 Crore rural households, in the country, around 15.89 Crore (82.09%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. State/ UT-wise details are at Annex . ‘Drinking Water’ is a state subject, and hence, the responsibility of planning, approval, implementation, operation and maintenance (O&M) of drinking water supply schemes, including those under the JJM, lies with State/ UT Governments. The Government of India supports the states by providing technical and financial assistance. All States/ UTs have been advised to notify comprehensive Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Policy in place with provisions for handing over of schemes to GPs/ VWSCs, empowering them to levy user charges, engaging women Self Help Groups (SHGs) for the collection of user charges, and undertaking O&M, and ensuring sufficient financing of O&M. The details of Gram Panchayat level collection of user charges are not maintained at Government of India level. In March 2026, the Union Cabinet has approved the extension of JJM period up to December 2028 with enhanced outlay and restructured implementation focusing on structural reforms in rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. The total financial outlay of the Mission has now been enhanced from ₹ 3.60 lakh crore to ₹ 8.69 lakh crore with the central share increasing from ₹ 2.08 lakh crore to ₹ 3.59 lakh crore i.e. additional central outlay of Rs. 1.51 lakh Crore. To ensure effective planning and execution under JJM 2.0, a structured and integrated framework viz. Comprehensive Implementation and Reform Plan (CIRP) are to be prepared by each State/ UT. CIRP will serve as the principal guiding framework for mission planning, prioritization, scheme and reform implementation, fund allocation and monitoring. title: KOSI-MECHI INTRA-STATE LINK PROJECT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti KOSI-MECHI INTRA-STATE LINK PROJECT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi The Kosi–Mechi Intra-State Link Project has been included under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayi Yojana – Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (PMKSY-AIBP) for balance cost of works of Rs. 6,143.22 crore, with central assistance of Rs. 3,652.56 crore. The project is scheduled for completion by March 2029.  The remodeling work of Eastern Kosi Main Canal from K.M. 0.00 to 41.30 has been taken up at an awarded contract value Rs. 2639.80 crore.  Physical progress of 8.5% has been achieved so far. The Government of India is engaged in regular dialogue with the Government of Nepal regarding construction of dams on the Kosi River for the mutual benefit of both countries, including flood control. A Joint Project Office (JPO-SKSKI) was constituted in 2003 with the mandate to prepare the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Sapta-Kosi Multipurpose Project and Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project. The status of preparation the DPRs of these projects is as under. Sapta Kosi Multipurpose Project: The work of topographical surveys, construction material survey, water quality survey, inland navigation studies, hydrological studies, seismological studies, drilling (1,258m), communication survey, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) studies have been completed. Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project: The work of topographical surveys, water quality survey, hydrological studies, seismological studies, drilling (1,549m), communication survey, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) studies have been completed for Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project. Further, no meeting of Indo-Nepal Joint Committee was held during 2025-26. Central assistance of Rs. 206.77 Crore has been released to the State of Bihar under the Flood Management and Border Areas Programme during last three years. No proposal for a permanent Kosi-Gandak basin authority is under consideration of the Government of India. The information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. *** ND (Rajya Sabha USQ 879) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289931) आगंतुक पटल  : 338 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali Ministry of Jal Shakti KOSI-MECHI INTRA-STATE LINK PROJECT प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT AND TECHNICAL PROGRESS OF THE KALPASAR PROJECT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT AND TECHNICAL PROGRESS OF THE KALPASAR PROJECT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi As informed by the Government of Gujarat, the proposed Gulf of Khambhat (Kalpasar) Project is an ambitious water resources initiatives of the State Government. The project envisages the creation of one of the world's largest coastal freshwater reservoirs through the construction of a dam across the Gulf of Khambhat. Upon implementation, the project is expected to significantly augment the availability of freshwater and substantially mitigate water scarcity in the Saurashtra region by providing a dependable source of water for irrigation and other identified uses. The project includes a proposed highway-cum-rail corridor over the dam across the Gulf of Khambhat. As per the present project layout, the corridor is expected to reduce the travel distance between Bhavnagar and Surat by approximately 179 km, from about 356 km through the existing land route to about 177 km via the proposed dyke corridor, thereby improving regional connectivity and reducing travel time. As informed by the State Government of Gujarat, Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Kalpasar Project is at an advanced stage of finalization. The ongoing Indo-Dutch technical cooperation is expected to further strengthen the DPR by incorporating international best practices and advanced technical expertise in areas such as coastal engineering, hydraulic modelling, salinity management, climate resilience and water management. This collaboration is intended to enhance the technical robustness of the project and facilitate informed decision-making during its implementation. The project envisages development of approximately 2,470 MW of hybrid renewable energy capacity on reclaimed land that is presently submerged during high tide. The renewable energy generated is proposed to be utilized, inter alia, for pumping freshwater to meet irrigation requirements in the coastal regions of Saurashtra. DPR incorporates appropriate engineering measures, hydraulic studies and salinity management strategies to address the issue of salinity ingress. The information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. *** ND (Rajya Sabha USQ 885) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289927) आगंतुक पटल  : 281 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Jal Shakti SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT AND TECHNICAL PROGRESS OF THE KALPASAR PROJECT प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: EXPANSION OF HEALTHCARE FACILITIES BY ESIC
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Labour & Employment EXPANSION OF HEALTHCARE FACILITIES BY ESIC Over 1.38 lakh new employers and more than 1.12 lakh new employees added under SPREE Scheme between July 2025 and January 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has launched the Scheme to Promote Registration of Employers/Employees (SPREE 2025) from July 2025 to January 2026.  Under the Scheme, a one-time opportunity was provided to employers and employees of organised sectors who may have been inadvertently left out from ESI coverage to register without concern for retrospective coverage or punitive action. A total of 1,38,718 new employers and 1,12,72,772 employees have been added during the Scheme till 31.01.2026. ESIC has undertaken several initiatives across the country to strengthen healthcare infrastructure, improve access to quality medical services and enhance social security benefits for ESI beneficiaries. These include enhancement of bed strength, procurement of advanced medical equipment, establishment of ICU/HDU facilities, operationalisation of new hospitals and dispensaries, empanelment of private and super-specialty hospitals, upgradation of digital platforms for OPD appointments, Aadhaar-based authentication for delivery of benefits, online submission of cash benefit claims, collaboration with Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) for providing secondary and tertiary healthcare services where ESIC facilities are not adequately available. ESIC has also recently operationalised/upgraded hospitals at Ompora (Jammu & Kashmir), Doddaballapur (Karnataka), Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu), Surat (Gujarat), and expanded hospitals at Sanath Nagar (Telangana), Beltola (Assam) and Rajamahendravaram (Andhra Pradesh). This information was given by the Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. ***** Rini Choudhury/Anjelina Alexander (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289945) आगंतुक पटल  : 180 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Labour & Employment EXPANSION OF HEALTHCARE FACILITIES BY ESIC Over 1.38 lakh new employers and more than 1.12 lakh new employees added under SPREE Scheme between July 2025 and January 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: SPECIAL DRIVE FOR THE EXPEDITIOUS DISPOSAL OF LONG-PENDING LABOUR CASES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Labour & Employment SPECIAL DRIVE FOR THE EXPEDITIOUS DISPOSAL OF LONG-PENDING LABOUR CASES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) has launched a three-month Special Drive from 1 st June, 2026 to 31 st August, 2026 for the expeditious disposal of pending industrial dispute cases and claim cases relating to wages, gratuity, maternity benefits and other statutory claims. title: ATAL BEEMIT VYAKTI KALYAN YOJANA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Labour & Employment ATAL BEEMIT VYAKTI KALYAN YOJANA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi The Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has approved extension of the Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) from 01.07.2026 to 30.06.2027. The eligibility criteria to avail benefit under the Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) is as under: The insured person must be in insurable employment for a minimum period of 12 months immediately before his/her unemployment and should have contributed for not less than 78 days in one completed contribution period in 12 months immediately preceding to unemployment. The unemployment must not arise from misconduct, during lock out, superannuation, or convicted for false statement under the provision of ESI Act, 1948. Several steps to expedite the settlement of claim under the scheme have been taken. These include online submission and processing of the claims, direct benefit transfer (DBT) to the bank accounts of beneficiaries and regular monitoring of claim settlement to ensure timely disbursal of benefits. title: Shri Keshav Chandra, IAS, Assumes Charge as Secretary, Ministry of Mines
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Mines Shri Keshav Chandra, IAS, Assumes Charge as Secretary, Ministry of Mines प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 12:55PM by PIB Delhi Shri Keshav Chandra, IAS (1995: AGMUT), today assumed charge as Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Government of India. Soon after assuming charge, Secretary Mines chaired a meeting with senior officials of the Ministry of Mines and reviewed the key initiatives and ongoing activities of the Ministry. During the meeting, senior officials briefed the Secretary on various important programmes and initiatives of the Ministry, including those related to mineral exploration, auction and operationalisation of mineral blocks, critical and strategic minerals, and other key areas of the mining and mineral sector. Secretary Mines emphasised the importance of coordinated efforts and effective implementation of the Ministry’s key initiatives to strengthen India’s mineral sector. *** PKMV (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289798) आगंतुक पटल  : 936 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Mines Shri Keshav Chandra, IAS, Assumes Charge as Secretary, Ministry of Mines प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: INSTITUTIONAL OUTREACH BY THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR MINORITIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs INSTITUTIONAL OUTREACH BY THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR MINORITIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 2:59PM by PIB Delhi NCM has conducted a study on the subject “ Contribution of Jain Community in the Field of Education” during 2026. The study documents the historical evolution, institutional contribution and educational philosophy of the Jain community in India. It captures the role of Jain trusts, philanthropists, educational institutions and community organisations in promoting learning, research, scholarships, value-based education and inclusive access to education. National Commission for Minorities (NCM), in discharge of its advisory and facilitative mandate, organized Conference of State Minorities Commissions on 19 May 2026 at New Delhi, which was attended by representatives of State Minorities Commissions, along with officials of State Governments and Union Territories. The Conference served as a platform to deliberate on institutional strengthening, administrative coordination, grievance redressal mechanisms, and the exchange of best practices for enhancing outreach and improving the delivery of welfare measures for minority communities. Annexure Annexure to part(a) of Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No 912 for answer on 27.07.2026 on the subject “Institutional Outreach by the National Commission for Minorities” Details of the seminars, conference and outreach progammes organized by National Commission for Minorities during 2026 National Seminar on "Buddhism in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Social Pathways" (27.02.2026, New Delhi) The National Commission for Minorities (NCM) organized a national seminar on “Buddhism in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Social Pathways” on 27.02.2026 in New Delhi. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of Minority Affairs, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar focused on heritage preservation, education, youth engagement and the role of Buddhist philosophy in promoting peace and social harmony. The seminar brought together policymakers, scholars, spiritual leaders, and community representatives to deliberate on the evolving role of Buddhism in India’s socio-cultural landscape. National Seminar on "The Contribution of the Jain Community to the Indian Economy, Education and Philanthropy" (23.04.2026, Indore) National Commission for Minorities (NCM), in collaboration with Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya (DAVV), Indore, organized a National Seminar on “The Contribution of the Jain Community to the Indian Economy, Education, and Philanthropy” on 23.4.2026 in Indore. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar brought together scholars, academicians, industrialists, philanthropists, students, and members of the Jain community to discuss the community’s significant role in nation-building. National Seminar on "Parsis in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Socio-Economic Pathways" (09.05.2026, Mumbai) National Commission for Minorities (NCM) organized a National Seminar on “Parsis in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Socio-Economic Pathways” on 09.05.2026 in Mumbai. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of Minority Affairs, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar focused on the preservation of Parsi heritage, socio-economic development, demographic challenges and the community's invaluable contribution to nation-building. The seminar brought together ministers, policymakers, scholars, industrialists, academicians, and members of the Parsi community to discuss issues related to cultural preservation, demographic challenges, and socio-economic development. Conference of State Minorities Commissions (19.05.2026, New Delhi) National Commission for Minorities organized the Conference of State Minorities Commissions on 19 th May 2026 at New Delhi to discuss minority welfare, protection of minority rights and inclusive development. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of Minority Affairs, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The Conference deliberated on best practices, challenges faced by State Commissions and the role of minority communities in nation-building. The conference brought together representatives from State Minorities Commissions, State Governments, Union Territories and minority communities to strengthen coordination and welfare mechanisms across the country. title: IMPACT OF PRADHAN MANTRI JAN VIKAS KARYAKRAM (PMJVK) ON MINORITIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs IMPACT OF PRADHAN MANTRI JAN VIKAS KARYAKRAM (PMJVK) ON MINORITIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 2:57PM by PIB Delhi Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Minority Affairs for creation of community infrastructure in the Minority Concentration Areas across the country in the sectors viz. title: PARTICIPATION OF SIKH COMMUNITIES IN PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS AND GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs PARTICIPATION OF SIKH COMMUNITIES IN PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS AND GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Minority Affairs implements various schemes to improve the socio-economic condition of the minority communities including Sikh community through affirmative action and inclusive development to facilitate an equitable share for minority communities in education, employment, economic activities and to ensure their upliftment ensuring dignity and equal participation. The Ministry is implementing various schemes like Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS), Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK), loans at lower interest rates through National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC). Recently Sh. Harjit Singh Grewal from the Sikh Community has been appointed as the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities (NCM). A Study on ‘Outreach to the Sikh community’ was conducted by the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) to better understand the unique challenges faced by this community. The purpose of the study was to identify gaps in current outreach efforts and recommend strategies to improve support, inclusivity, and engagement for the Sikh community in various social, cultural, and economic sectors. To promote social harmony and mutual understanding among different religious communities, National Commission for Minorities (NCM) regularly organizes Sarv Dharm Samvad (interfaith dialogue) meetings with representatives of minority communities and celebrated major festivals of minority religions. The Commission also advises all States/ UTs to institutionalize periodic Sarv Dharm Samvad meetings and Sarv Dharm Sadbhav events involving religious leaders, community representatives, NGOs, and government officials to promote social harmony, interfaith dialogue, and mutual understanding. These initiatives help address the minority concerns, create awareness, and ensure the effective implementation of government welfare schemes for minority communities. This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ***** AK/MR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289849) आगंतुक पटल  : 157 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Minority Affairs PARTICIPATION OF SIKH COMMUNITIES IN PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS AND GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Launches Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, SAMARTH Portal & Releases Model OSR Rules to Strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions in India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Panchayati Raj Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Launches Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, SAMARTH Portal & Releases Model OSR Rules to Strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions in India Self-Reliant Panchayats Key to Realizing the Vision of Viksit Bharat @2047”: Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program Will Turn Local Assets into Sustainable Revenue-Generating Projects; SAMARTH Portal to Strengthen Efficiency in Panchayat Revenue Collection; Model OSR Rules to Provide Guiding Framework for States to Strengthen Panchayat Revenues प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 JUL 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Panchayati Raj and Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, launched the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme, the SAMARTH Panchayat Portal and released the Model OSR (Own Source of Revenue) Rules for Panchayati Raj Institutions at a function held at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. On this occasion, the Union Minister was also presented with the Trophy and Certificate for the Gold Award conferred on the Ministry under the National Awards for e-Governance (NAeG) 2026 for the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) – Data Driven Governance for Viksit Bharat. Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Union Minister of State for Panchayati Raj, Shri Vivek Bharadwaj, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj along with other senior officers of the Ministry were also present on the occasion. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh said that the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme, SAMARTH Panchayat Portal and Model OSR Rules mark a significant step towards building financially empowered, technologically enabled and self-reliant Panchayats, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. He said that Panchayati Raj Institutions are central to India’s democratic and developmental journey. Strengthening them with digital tools and sustainable revenue streams would improve grassroots governance and accelerate inclusive rural development. The Union Minister said that the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme would enable Panchayats to identify local assets and opportunities and convert them into sustainable revenue-generating projects. He stated that, the SAMARTH Panchayat Portal would facilitate seamless and transparent taxation, payments and monitoring of Panchayat revenues.  The Union Minister observed that these initiatives are aligned with the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission on strengthening Own Source Revenue (OSR). Shri Singh urged elected representatives and functionaries of PRIs and RLBs to make effective use of these initiatives to further enhance transparency, strengthen participatory democracy and promote citizen-centric governance at the grassroots. Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme is a unique initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj that enables Gram Panchayats and Block Panchayats to identify local assets and opportunities and develop them, with dedicated technical support from the Ministry, into bankable, revenue-generating projects that build sustainable OSR. Financing is facilitated through Public Private Partnerships, Corporate Social Responsibility contributions, convergence with other schemes and bank finance, with NABARD and HUDCO as institutional partners. A total of 350 projects are to be developed over four years, comprising 50 projects in the first year and 100 in each of the following three years. Gram Panchayats with a minimum OSR of Rs. 50 lakh and Block Panchayats with a minimum OSR of Rs. 1 crore, each with at least three years of tenure remaining, are eligible to apply, with relaxed thresholds for special category States. Outreach workshops on the programme have been held for Panchayat representatives across ten States, till date. For More details visit: https://egramswaraj.gov.in/atmanibharguidelines.do / Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program SAMARTH Panchayat Portal The SAMARTH Panchayat Portal is a first-of-its-kind digital initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj designed to strengthen the financial capacity of Gram Panchayats through technology-enabled management of OSR. Developed as a unified, configurable national platform, SAMARTH enables Gram Panchayats to digitally manage the complete OSR lifecycle, from taxpayer registration and demand generation to online payments, collection and real-time monitoring. The launch complements the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, which has emphasized strengthening the OSR of PRIs/ RLBs to improve their financial sustainability. Chhattisgarh and Himachal Pradesh have already been onboarded on the portal, with more than 51 lakh taxpayers registered, demand notices worth Rs. 95 crore generated and over Rs. 27 crore collected to date. Onboarding is underway in Maharashtra, Mizoram, Assam, Haryana, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh. For More details visit: www.samarthpanchayat.gov.in / SAMARTH Panchayat Portal Model OSR Rules for Panchayati Raj Institutions To strengthen the financial independence of Panchayati Raj Institutions, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj has prepared Model OSR (Own Sources of Revenue) Rules as a guiding framework for States and Union Territories. Building on the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the Model Rules aim to support States in creating a transparent, uniform and efficient system for the assessment, collection and management of Panchayat revenues such as property tax, user charges, fees and other non-tax revenues. These Model Rules are advisory in nature and may be adopted or adapted by States according to their local requirements and existing legal framework. The initiative seeks to promote better revenue mobilization, strengthen local governance and enable Panchayats to become more financially self-reliant while improving service delivery to rural citizens. Recognition at National e-Governance Awards 2026 Four Panchayati Raj related initiatives, including the Panchayat Advancement Index, were conferred National Awards for e-Governance 2026, comprising three Gold and one Silver, at the 29th National Conference on e-Governance held in Jaipur from 1 to 2 July 2026, reflecting the Panchayati Raj sector’s expanding leadership in data driven, grassroots digital governance. **** AA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290029) आगंतुक पटल  : 241 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Malayalam Ministry of Panchayati Raj Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Launches Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, SAMARTH Portal & Releases Model OSR Rules to Strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions in India Self-Reliant Panchayats Key to Realizing the Vision of Viksit Bharat @2047”: Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program Will Turn Local Assets into Sustainable Revenue-Generating Projects; SAMARTH Portal to Strengthen Efficiency in Panchayat Revenue Collection; Model OSR Rules to Provide Guiding Framework for States to Strengthen Panchayat Revenues प्रविष्टि तिथि:
